## Forward Fill All Empty Values for CPI 
```{r}
df_clean <- data %>%
  arrange(coin, week) %>%
  mutate(week = dmy(week)) %>%
  mutate(
    cpi_lag1 = na.locf(cpi_lag1, na.rm = FALSE),
    cpi_inflation_mom_lag1 = na.locf(cpi_inflation_mom_lag1, na.rm = FALSE)
  )
```


## Filter out one coin
```{r}
df_clean_BCH <- df_clean %>%
  filter(coin == "BCH")

```

## ADF Test to Check for Stationarity 
```{r}
list_of_non_stationary_2 <- list()

df_clean_BCH_2 <- df_clean_BCH
# Loop through each variable (excluding date)
for (i in names(df_clean_BCH_2 %>% select(-c(1,2)))) {
  adf_p <- tryCatch(adf.test(df_clean_BCH_2[[i]], k = 0)$p.value,
    error = function(e) NA
  )
  if (!is.na(adf_p) && adf_p > 0.05) {
    list_of_non_stationary_2 <- c(list_of_non_stationary_2, i)
  }
}


# ADF test with trend
list_of_non_stationary_trend <- list()
for (i in 3:ncol(df_clean_BCH)) {
  test_stat <- tryCatch(ur.df(df_clean_BCH[[i]], type = "trend", selectlags = "AIC")@teststat[1],
    error = function(e) NA
  )
  critical_val <- tryCatch(ur.df(df_clean_BCH[[i]], type = "trend", selectlags = "AIC")@cval,
    error = function(e) NA
  )
  if (!is.na(test_stat) && !is.na(critical_val[2]) && test_stat > critical_val[2]) {
    list_of_non_stationary_trend <- c(list_of_non_stationary_trend, i)
  }
}

cat("Variables non-stationary without trend:\n")
print(unlist(list_of_non_stationary_2))
cat("Variables non-stationary with trend:\n")
print(unlist(list_of_non_stationary_trend))
```


## Random Forest Model - Rolling Window  
```{r}
runrf <- function(Y, indice, n_lags = 0, ntree, mtry) {
  Y2 <- Y
  
  #Use if we want to add additional lags 
  aux <- embed(Y2, n_lags + 1)
  
  # Target variable (already led, so take current column)
  y <- aux[, indice]
  
  #Predictors = lagged values only (drop target column)
  X <- aux[, -(indice)]
  
  #Latest observation for prediction
  X.out <- tail(X, 1)
  
  # Train model
  model <- randomForest(
    x = X,
    y = y,
    #Parameter Tuning for ntree 
    ntree = ntree,
    importance = TRUE, 
    mtry = mtry
  )
  
  #Predict
  pred <- predict(model, X.out)
  
  
  return(list(model = model, pred = pred))
}


#This function will repeatedly call the previous function in the rolling window h-step forecasting
#Inputs for the function:
#1) Data matrix Y: includes all variables
#2) nprev - number of out-of-sample observations (at the end of the sample)
#3) indice - indice of the location of y var
#4) ntree - number of trees to fit for the forest
#5) mtry - number of predictors to for the forest 


rf.rolling.window=function(Y,nprev,indice=1, ntree, mtry){
  save.importance=list() #blank for saving variable importance
  save.pred=matrix(NA,nprev,1) ##blank for forecasts
  for(i in nprev:1){#NB: backwards FOR loop: going from 180 down to 1
    Y.window=Y[(1+nprev-i):(nrow(Y)-i),] #define the estimation window (first one: 1 to 491, then 2 to 492 etc.)
    rf=runrf(Y.window,indice,0,ntree, mtry) #call the function to fit the Random Forest and generate h-step forecast
    save.pred[(1+nprev-i),]=rf$pred #save the forecast
    save.importance[[i]]=importance(rf$model) #save variable importance
    cat("iteration",(1+nprev-i),"\n") #display iteration number
  }
  
  real=Y[,indice]#get actual values
  #plot(real,type="l")
  #lines(c(rep(NA,length(real)-nprev),save.pred),col="red") #padded with NA for blanks, plot predictions vs. actual
  
  rmse=sqrt(mean((tail(real,nprev)-save.pred)^2)) #compute RMSE
  mae=mean(abs(tail(real,nprev)-save.pred)) #compute MAE (Mean Absolute Error)
  errors=c("rmse"=rmse,"mae"=mae) #stack errors in a vector
  
  return(list("pred"=save.pred,"errors"=errors,"save.importance"=save.importance)) #return forecasts, history of variable importance, and RMSE and MAE for the period.
}

```

```{r}
#Goes through mtry and ntree and selects best ntree based on lowest RMSE on validation Set 
rf.select_parameter = function(Y, nprev, indice = 1, parameters_ntree, parameters_mtry){
  rmse_all <- list()
  best_parameter <- NA 
  lowest_rmse <- Inf 
  for (i in parameters_ntree){
    for (j in parameters_mtry){
      curr_model = rf.rolling.window(Y, nprev, indice, i, j)
      print(i)
      rmse =curr_model$errors['rmse']
      preds = curr_model$pred 
      print(preds)
      rmse_all[[as.character(i)]]=rmse
      if (rmse <= lowest_rmse){
        best_parameter_ntree = i 
        best_parameter_mtry = j
        lowest_rmse <- rmse 
        print(lowest_rmse)
    }
    }
  }
  return(list(best_parameter_ntree, best_parameter_mtry, rmse_all))
}
```



```{r}
set.seed(4211)
#Extract unique coins 
all_coins <- c(unique(df_clean$coin))
results_all_coins = list()

#Number of train/test/valid
train_BCH_num = nrow(df_clean_BCH %>% filter(week <= "2022-12-30") %>%
  filter(week >= "2018-01-01"))

valid_BCH_num = nrow(df_clean_BCH %>% filter(week > "2022-12-30") %>%
  filter(week <= "2024-12-30"))

test_BCH_num = nrow(df_clean_BCH %>% filter(week > "2024-12-30") %>%
  filter(week <= "2026-01-08")) 

##Loop Through Each Coin, Find best parameter for ntree using validation set, predict on test set 
for (i in all_coins){
  coin_remove_var <- df_clean %>%
    filter(coin == i) 
  
  ## Create data for train and validation for parameter selection 
  train_valid_df = coin_remove_var %>% filter(week <= "2024-12-30") %>%
  filter(week >= "2018-01-01") %>%
  select(-c("week", "coin"))
  
  ## Training to select parameters 
  rf_train_data <- rf.select_parameter(as.matrix(train_valid_df), valid_BCH_num, indice = 1, c(10,1000), c(floor(47/3), 25, 35, 47))
  best_param_ntree <- rf_train_data[[1]]
  best_param_mtry <- rf_train_data[[2]]
  
  ## Create data for prediction 
  preds_df <- coin_remove_var %>%
    filter(week >= "2018-01-01") %>%
    filter(week < "2026-01-09") %>%
    tail(test_BCH_num + train_BCH_num) %>%
    select(-c("week", "coin"))
  
  ## Predict model based on best parameters
  model_preds <- rf.rolling.window(as.matrix(preds_df), test_BCH_num, indice = 1, best_param_ntree, best_param_mtry)
  
  results_all_coins[[i]] <- list(
  model_preds = model_preds,
  best_ntree = best_param_ntree,
  best_mtry = best_param_mtry
)
  
  saveRDS(results_all_coins, "results_all_coins.rds")
  
}


```

```{r}
MSE <- function(pred, truth){ #start and end body of the function by { } - same as a loop 
  return(summary(lm((truth-pred)^2~1))$coef[1:2]) #end function with a return(output) statement. Here we can go straight to return because the object of interest is a simple function of inputs
}
rft.pred = predict(rftune, newdata=x3)
cbind(rft.pred, y3)
MSE(rft.pred,y3)
```


```{r}
library(car)

vif_with_alias_fix <- function(formula, data, threshold = 10) {
  # Step 1: Fit initial model
  model <- lm(formula, data = data)
  
  # Step 2: Detect aliased (perfectly collinear) variables
  aliased <- alias(model)$Complete
  removed_vars <- rownames(aliased)
  
  if (length(removed_vars) > 0) {
    cat("Removed aliased variables:\n")
    print(removed_vars)
    
    # Remove them from the dataset
    data <- data[, !colnames(data) %in% removed_vars]
    
    # Refit model
    model <- lm(formula, data = data)
  } else {
    cat("No aliased variables detected.\n")
  }
  
  # Step 3: Compute VIFs
  vifs <- vif(model)
  
  # Step 4: Print variables with VIF > threshold
  high_vif <- vifs[vifs > threshold]
  if (length(high_vif) == 0) {
    cat("No variables with VIF >", threshold, "\n")
  } else {
    cat("Variables with VIF >", threshold, ":\n")
    print(high_vif)
  }
  
  # Step 5: Return model and removed variables
  return(list(model = model, removed_alias = removed_vars, high_vif = high_vif))
}


```
